newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson included Saudi deal in sale papers.
newsitem.headline: Thomson included Saudi deal in sale papers.

text.p: Thomson-CSF had included the prospect of selling a third frigate to Saudi Arabia in information made available to bidders Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere in its privatisation, a Thomson-CSF spokesman said.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe announced on Tuesday the sale of the frigate along with weapons systems and extra equipment for two frigates ordered by Saudi Arabia in November 1994.
The new contract is estimated at eight billion francs, with over half going to prime contractor Thomson-CSF, a source familiar with the deal said.

"The (privatisation) candidates have had in the last few weeks confidential information on the outlook for orders in the coming years. The possibility of this contract had been indicated at this time and has been taken into account by the candidates," the spokesman said.
The order will appear in the first half 1997 order book but will not have an effect on the group's results this year.
Thomson-CSF is the prime contractor for the contract which involves work for the state-owned DCN naval shipyard and Aerospatiale, which is supplying the anti-missile Arabel-Aster missile system.
The sale is an extension of the Sawari 2 contract which covers the delivery by 2004 of two F3000 air defence frigates based on the French navy's La Fayette class.
